questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: As a french-speaking person I was looking to study abroad far away (from europe) in a french-speaking city as Montreal. As McGill is the biggest university i didn't hesitate much.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It can be overwhleming with all the information in the beginning because there is different website you need to see but they assist you well.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Upon arrival you'll get emails and links to websites where tou can join events where a lot of crucial information will be given.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: For me it was quite easy through a renting company called "Hello Montreal" which is specialised in renting to international students. There are a lot of international students you can find housing on facebook quite easily.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus can mean you need some time to get there they have busses and metro but if you don't live close by a metro station it can take quite some time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You first search through the courses on their course catalogue. Then the registration period opens up and you can fin the course on minerva and just register online. As an exchange student your regsitration period starts after some other students so some courses might be full before you even can register. In that case there can be a waitlist or you can check the site often to see if someone unregistered leaving a empty seat.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can write to your department for help for some courses it is needed to write before trying to register and they can also grant you permissions for some courses where there is prerequisites.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Every course i wanted was full when i started the registering process, but got got accepted in them all before the end of the summer vacation by checking minerva nearly every day.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register as soon as possible and check minerva often.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The difficulty of a course varies a lot from course to course but for me it was pretty much the same difficulty as in KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Teaching was also similar with hand ins and exercise. Note that they have a midterm and your grade is often depending on the work delivered through the whole course and not on the final exam. But this also varies from course to course.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
COMP 557 - Fundamentals of Comp. Graphics
COMP 424 - Artificial Intelligence
COMP 360 - Algorithm Design
PHIL 230 - Intro to Moral Philosophy 1

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: COMP 424 - Artificial Intelligence is very interesting and not as hard as one could imagine.

questions.answer: A visit at the hospital can get very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lots of associations but i wasn't part of any of them.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: They had a outdoor association which seemed cool.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: You can visit some nice lakes and mountains one or two hour drive away from Montreal.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy they are very open and there is people from everywhere.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the events in the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Their french accent.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The diversity and open mindset.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: To be on time and willing to write some mails for the registration phase. Don't get overwhelmed by all the administrative work. And enjoy!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It gets really cold from the start of december.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making new friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Leave. And to keep up with the courses.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
